# Policy-KB bijection audit — employee_meal_account_desk / task 1

Scope: the whole normative domain of the `meal` product charter as this difficulty extends it — `tasks/employee_meal_account_desk/meal.extended.yaml` (10 base policies with their eligibilities, 6 extended policies with 9 `overwrite` declarations, 30 declared factors, 5 `prerequisite` edges, 6 variants × 50 parameters + 4 entry-gate fields), `task_tools.py` (6 task tools), against the 64 published documents of `docs/meal/`. The scan is of the whole domain, not of the branch this seed hits: the three problems of task 0's tree, the untriggered tiers of all 30 ladders and the retired surface are all covered here as well.

Entry conditions cited, not re-run: the policy-side verdict for this difficulty is PASS (closed at round 3); `check_docs.py … meal` → `DOCS OK` (64 docs, roles factor 30 / baseline 6 / facet 10 / policy 12 / hub 6, 95 required quantitative keys, 6 task tools, 5 prerequisite edges, mechanical gates PASS, semantic bijection MANUAL REQUIRED); `check_traceability.py …/tasks/employee_meal_account_desk` → `TRACEABILITY OK` (0.json 15/0 True, 1.json 17/0 True). The runtime-visible view and a tool-shaped DB access path were supplied and used. Nothing is missing on the input side.

**Resolution basis for this task's two edges — the sentence, the depended-on rule, and the records.**

- **Edge 1** names the state *"the largest till transaction rung against payroll on the account carries the allowance application it is owed"*. The depended-on policy's hub states, in those same words, the write that brings it about: `spending_allowance_against_a_till_transaction_8465c97b.json` — "**One application entry is booked** for the whole of the allowance applied to a **till transaction**, whatever lots it draws on … The call books an allowance application entry on the account's transaction ledger for the value stated and **marks it with the till transaction it meets**", with `original_pos_reference` as the naming parameter. The records close the loop: the largest payroll meal is `POS-51002076` ($21.40, 2026-05-27) and no `subsidy_application` row carries that `original_pos_reference`. The hop is resolvable at the source's strength from the sentence, the depended-on rule and the records alone.
- **Edge 2** names the state *"the allowance lot the account is owed for the current grant period stands on its ledger"*. `placing_an_allowance_lot_on_an_account_f518c2ea.json` states the write in the sentence's own words — "The call books an **allowance grant entry** on the account's transaction ledger for the value stated, **mints the allowance lot reference** that entry is traced under, and raises the unspent employer allowance standing on the account by the same value" — and `allowance_grant_schedule_d2d6f638.json` fixes what "the current grant period" is for this plan ("Allowance granted: each service day"; "A lot stays spendable for: 1 calendar day"), which together with the dated `subsidy_grant` rows makes the state decidable.

**The depended-on side never discloses who waits on it.** Neither `spending_allowance_against_a_till_transaction_8465c97b.json` nor `placing_an_allowance_lot_on_an_account_f518c2ea.json` carries the sentence of the policy that waits on it — the first carries only its *own* prerequisite sentence (edge 2, where it is the blocked side), and the second carries none. `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` and `fallback_reason` appear in no document.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the 64 documents was traced to a structured source. Three findings and one low-weight addition; the policy-side observations are listed separately.

### S1 — `KB-BIJECTION RED`: the per-plan entry-gate conditions are unborne

**Symptom → root cause.** Three of the four dimensions of the entry gate are named as dimensions and never given values, because the render carries the tenure dimension (duplicated into `parameters` as `tier_entry_min_tenure_months`) and drops the three booleans that live only in `variants[].entry_gate`.

**Evidence.** Source `meal_enrollment_terms`: "An employee is enrolled onto the highest meal plan whose entry gate they meet on length of service, on whether their employer runs the programme, on whether payroll consent has been given and on whether a manager has approved"; "Plans that require payroll consent are not activated until that consent is recorded, and until then the account stays enrolled and the badge is declined at the till." Source `meal_plan_change_terms`: "Where the employee does not meet the entry gate of the plan asked for, the change is declined and the highest plan whose gate they do meet is offered instead." Source values — `requires_employer_program`: false, true, true, true, true, true; `requires_payroll_consent`: false, false, true, true, false, true; `requires_manager_approval`: false, false, false, false, true, true. KB: `enrolment_and_badge_conditions_2bd6557e.json` §1 and §4 and `moving_between_meal_plans_08de3142.json` name the dimensions generically; `plan_entry_and_badge_schedule_ace7b64f.json` prints only the tenure column. A search of all five product corpora for "manager", "payroll consent" and "employer runs the programme" returns only generic mentions in those three documents.

**Consequence.** "The account is opened on the highest plan whose service requirement they do meet" is decidable from the visible materials; "the highest meal plan whose entry gate they meet" and "the highest plan whose gate they do meet is offered instead" are not, for three of the four dimensions.

**Affected documents and locations.** `docs/meal/plan_entry_and_badge_schedule_ace7b64f.json` (schedule table + "What each column means"); `docs/meal/enrolment_and_badge_conditions_2bd6557e.json` §1, §4; `docs/meal/moving_between_meal_plans_08de3142.json` ("When a change is accepted", "Where the gate is not met").

**Effect on this task.** None — this task neither opens, activates nor changes a plan. Recorded under the skill's rule that an omitted branch is RED even where the seed's numbers are unaffected.

### S2 — `KB-BIJECTION RED`: an unsourced per-plan claim that the document's own table contradicts

**Evidence.** `docs/meal/plan_entry_and_badge_schedule_ace7b64f.json`, "Points of judgement": "**The two plans printing no entry service, no enrolment charge and no manager approval are the open end of the line**; the Executive Dining Charge Account, printing 12 months of service and a $25.00 charge, is the closed end."

- "no manager approval" is an entry-gate fact (`requires_manager_approval`) that the table does not carry and that no document states plan by plan — S1 surfacing as a positive claim.
- Against the document's own figures: plans printing 0 months of service are the Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account and the Prepaid Declining Balance Account; of those only the Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account prints $0.00 to open (the Prepaid Declining Balance Account prints $5.00). The conjunction holds for exactly **one** plan, not two.

**Root cause.** A descriptive generalisation across the schedule that is neither a source atom nor a derivation provable from the schedule.

**Affected document and location.** `docs/meal/plan_entry_and_badge_schedule_ace7b64f.json`, "Points of judgement", sentence 1.

### S3 — `KB-BIJECTION RED`: a per-variant parameter rendered as a line-wide constant

**Evidence.** `docs/meal/holding_accounts_at_several_sites_88ec232b.json`, "The ceiling on accounts held": "No employee holds more than the number of accounts printed against the meal plan at once, counting every account that is enrolled, active, restricted or suspended; **the ceiling this line works to is 2 accounts**." Source `max_accounts_per_employee` = 2, 2, 2, 2, **1**, **1**. The first half of the sentence is the source's own clause and is exact; the appended clause states a line-wide ceiling the source does not have and that is wrong for the Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account and the Executive Dining Charge Account. The per-plan column is printed correctly in `plan_entry_and_badge_schedule_ace7b64f.json`, so the two documents can be reconciled by a reader who holds both; a reader who holds only this one is told the wrong ceiling for two of six plans.

**Affected document and location.** `docs/meal/holding_accounts_at_several_sites_88ec232b.json`, "The ceiling on accounts held", sentence 1.

### S4 — addition: a discretionary condition with no structured source

**Evidence.** `docs/meal/taking_a_spending_restriction_off_an_account_95f07956.json`, opening: "Where a spending restriction stands on an Employee Meal Account **and the desk is satisfied it should come off** …". The source rule opens "When a spending restriction is taken off an employee meal account, the charges the account carries forward are restated on the spot …". No source atom makes the desk's satisfaction a condition. **Weight: low** — the clause creates no obligation, names no review, confirmation or notification, and neither hardens nor softens a gate the source sets. It belongs to task 0's root problem; recorded here because this scan is of the whole domain.

### S5 — policy-side note: the baseline hints at its own variation

**Evidence.** `docs/meal/payroll_charge_calculation_d6ef3365.json` §3 — this task's root computation: "No account is taken of the stored value the employee already holds. The stored value taken into account is never moved from the account: it stays spendable, the meals it will meet are never charged to payroll, **and that is why the charge carried is net of it**." Both sentences are the source's own (`meal_ext_payroll_charge_consent`'s rule, in that order), so the KB may drop neither and the rendering is faithful. As published, however, a baseline that zeroes a term and then explains why the result is net of it does signal to a reader that the term varies — which the corpus's discrete-topology design otherwise avoids. The comparable rationale sentences of the same policy and of `meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown` were homed in their factor documents instead ("A refund that restores employer allowance is never credited here…" → `refunds_credited_against_meals_carried_60e78763.json`; "A guest meal is charged to payroll net of the guest surcharge…" → `guest_surcharge_carried_into_a_paydown_1425a891.json`), so the placement is not uniform. Per Step 4 this is recorded as a policy-side note and does not change this skill's verdict.

### The two prerequisite-side checks the reverse scan requires

- **Cross-problem operational guidance:** none. Each of the six task-tool names occurs in exactly one document, its own policy's hub, inside that hub's own invocation block. In particular `consenting_to_a_meal_charge_against_pay_0af2277f.json` names only `confirm_payroll_charge_accrual_6d54e4b8`, and `spending_allowance_against_a_till_transaction_8465c97b.json` names only `apply_allowance_to_ticket_3fbfdeca` — neither names the tool of the problem it waits on. No document says "if unmet, first call …", names a resolving action beside a state-form sentence, or names a policy id. A pattern sweep for pointer and route language returned two benign hits only (an in-policy eligibility checklist; a `POS-` format string in a tool's own parameter row).
- **A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact:** none. No document names a customer, a site or venue code, a POS or lot reference, a balance or a status from either task's world. Every illustration is flagged hypothetical and uses deliberately unlike figures ($16.00 tickets, $95.00 lots, $64.00 stored value, $46.00 of applications, $27.00 netted off, 40/200-day-old loads).

### Policy-side notes (reported, not counted toward this skill's verdict)

- **N-a — prose and compute part company on whether a guest meal is "a meal rung against payroll".** The source rule of this task's root and middle computations says "the largest meal rung against payroll on the account" and "those rung against payroll in the last three calendar months"; the scored `compute` reads `transaction_code='meal_purchase', payment_channel='payroll_deduction'`, excluding `guest_meal` rows. The KB carries the prose faithfully — `allowance_application_calculation_8d744c5e.json` §1 and `stretch_of_meals_carried_to_pay_cfc2fe49.json` name only the payroll-tender test — and so inherits the gap, while the same source uses the distinct phrase "meals of the employee's own" where it means to exclude guests and the KB renders *that* exclusion explicitly (`restoring_a_working_balance_at_the_till_18031ccf.json`: "What is counted is meals of the employee's own, not guest meals and not allowance applications"). In this task the divergence changes nothing, because both guest meals are badge taps rather than payroll tenders; in the sibling task's world two guest meals **are** rung against payroll, so the ambiguity is live in this scenario's data. Origin is the source's prose/compute mismatch, not the translation.
- **N-b — the user tool's schema keeps the framing the extended rule replaced.** `load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b`'s docstring, visible at runtime, says the value "stands to your credit against what you owe", while the extended rule leaves the charges awaiting recovery untouched. The KB adjudicates this correctly and twice (`paying_in_to_lift_a_spending_restriction_8160ec82.json`; `charges_carried_forward_at_reinstatement_323cfbf9.json` §2). Tool-contract matter, outside this skill.
- **N-c — a residue of the retired "share of arrears" framing survives in a base clause** that the source did not declare retired, and that the KB therefore correctly carries in force (`switching_payroll_tender_off_and_on_bd89b99a.json`: "Where the plan requires the whole balance paid, a part payment does not lift the restriction however large it is").
- **N-d — "last calendar month" / "last three calendar months" are never defined** as rolling windows versus named calendar months, in the source or in the KB. The blind derivation read them as rolling and matched GT on all six scored values, so the reading is settled in practice; the source leaves it open and the KB rightly does not close what the source leaves open.

### The two declined notes

**N-e — the counting basis of the month windows. Declining was right; the gap is real and should be routed to the source layer.**

The renderer's premise checks out on the charter: `temporal_basis` and `counting_rule` appear **twice each in `policies` and zero times in `extended_policies`**. The two are the `refund_window` and `balance_return_window` eligibilities, each carrying clock, anchor event, anchor source, relation, duration source, unit, an explicit counting rule and an inclusive boundary — all of which the KB renders faithfully. So the charter fixes a counting basis where it means to, and fixes nothing for the month windows every extended policy relies on.

On the translation question the renderer is right, and this skill says it outright: *"where the source leaves it open, the documents may not close it either (render Value 0)."* Publishing the harness's arithmetic convention would be a boundary rule with no policy locator — added policy, and the "dissolve the contradiction by hiding one side" that Step 4 forbids.

The openness is nevertheless **outcome-determining**, which deserves to be said more sharply than revision 1 said it. Two demonstrations from this difficulty's own worlds, from published sentences only:

- *This task.* `stretch_of_meals_carried_to_pay_cfc2fe49.json` sums "those rung against payroll in the last three calendar months", with the clock at 2026-06-11. Read as a trailing window, the meals carried come to $99.30. Read as the three completed named months — March, April, May — the June meals of 2026-06-03 and 2026-06-09 drop out and the figure is $72.15. The charge the employee consents to moves with it.
- *The sibling task.* `deferral_of_recovery_after_short_tenders_870caaf1.json` bands on "overdraft charges … raised on it in the last three calendar months", with overdraft charges on 2026-02-13 and 2026-03-09 and the clock at 2026-03-17. Trailing: both in, "2 or more → $45.00". Completed named months (December, January, February): only one in, "Exactly 1 → $20.00" — a $25.00 swing that carries into the paydown and the restated figure.

So a careful reader taking the other defensible reading reaches different numbers in both tasks. **I agree this is a source gap and say so plainly: the extended policies should fix the counting basis the way the two base time eligibilities do.** It changes no verdict of this skill and does not reopen either blind audit — revision 1's derivation took the trailing reading, gave its grounds from published text (the corpus's day windows — 90-day recent load, 45-day recovery recency, "a restriction standing 21 days" — are all trailing from the clock) and landed on gold on all six scored values.

**N-a — declining to narrow "meal rung against payroll". The reasoning is correct.**

Narrowing the published phrase to match a compute filter would be the KB deciding a question the source has not decided, and would hide a source-layer divergence inside the documents — the named anti-pattern of Step 4. Two things sharpen the point in the renderer's favour: the charter itself uses a *different* phrase, "meals of the employee's own", wherever it does mean to exclude guests, and the KB renders that exclusion explicitly there (`restoring_a_working_balance_at_the_till_18031ccf.json`), so the vocabulary existed and simply was not used in these two places; and the divergence is live in this difficulty's data, since the sibling task's ledger carries two guest meals rung against payroll. It remains outcome-neutral in both tasks — this task's guest meals are badge taps, and the sibling's computations read charges accrued rather than meals. Source-layer item; the auditor does not say whether the rule text or the compute should move.

**The four items recorded as source-side or out of domain** — the `load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b` docstring residue, the un-retired base clause, the GT narrative slip, and the baseline-sentence placement question — match revision 1's dispositions, and declining each is right; retiring a clause the source never declared retired would be the KB legislating. On the placement question (**S5**): the renderer's ground — both sentences are that policy's `baseline.rule` and the computation document is the declared home of every baseline sentence — is sound and is why no verdict attaches. It does not by itself explain why the same policy's refund-exclusion sentence, in the identical structural position, was homed in the factor document; the better reading is that the refund sentence qualifies *which refunds the factor counts* while the stored-value sentence explains the baseline term itself, on which both placements are right. ### Three observations, none of them a defect

**O1 — the boundary convention is published only in the six computation documents.** A factor document read alone now fixes the window's **anchor** but not its **inclusivity at the exact boundary**. Not a defect: the source writes the counting rule into each `rule` and `baseline.rule` and into **no ladder face**, so the render has homed it exactly where the source and the skill put it; adding it to 25 factor documents would mean writing a sentence onto ladder faces the source does not carry it on, and a factor document may not point at the computation document in any case. It is unreachable on both worlds — the closest any entry on either ledger comes to any boundary day is **one day** (the sibling task, 2026-02-18 against a 2026-02-17 boundary; on this task's ledger the nearest is four days, 2026-05-15 against 2026-05-11). Recorded so it can be re-checked, not as a finding.

**O2 — one seam left by the hand rewording.** `refunds_credited_against_meals_carried_60e78763.json` carries the source face exactly in its clause ("the three **calendar** months running back from the day the account is worked") but renders the same window as "the three **months** running back from the day the account is worked" in the band table's second row and in the illustration, while the table's *third* row keeps "calendar" — one table holding both spellings of one window. The qualifier is intact everywhere, the clause is exact, no tier, threshold or value is affected, and the corpus has no other month unit, so no reading diverges. It is the single visible seam in "reworded for readability, never for meaning". Location reported; no verdict, and no wording proposed.

**O3 — the counting-rule section sits in six baselines that themselves use no month window.** None of the six baselines invokes one ("to date", "that same balance standing", "the deduction ceiling printed against the plan", "nothing"), so a reader of a baseline alone may infer that month windows exist somewhere in the policy. Judged **not** a `KB-EXPLICIT RED`: the forbidden exemplars all assert or point at a variation, while this sentence asserts none, names none and points nowhere; and it is a source atom of each `baseline.rule` which the render must carry and which the skill homes in the computation document — dropping it would be `KB-BIJECTION RED`, and the render added nothing beyond its source. By the principle the skill applies to base-law sentences that state an order, the hook belongs to the source's choice to write a windows rule into policies whose baselines use no window. Recorded as a policy-side note with both sides given, so the judgement can be re-checked.

### The two referred observations

**N4-1 — the short-month boundary. Declining was right, and the case is unreachable by margin, not by assumption.** The rule turns on "a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again", which is undefined when the booked day has no counterpart in the target month. Publishing a disambiguation the source does not state would be the render adding a boundary rule with no policy locator — the same error the renderer correctly refused in round 2 before the locator existed; having gained one, it carried exactly what the locator says and no more. Consistent, and right.

Verified on the records: **this** task's ledger contains three entries booked later than the 28th — 2026-03-30, 2026-05-30 and 2026-05-31 — and they sit 19, 19 and 20 days inside their relevant boundaries, so no convention for "31 May plus one month" changes any inclusion. The sibling task's ledger contains none at all. Separately, no entry on either ledger falls on a boundary day. Whether the source's rule should resolve the short-month case is a source question, properly left as an observation there.

**N4-2 — `duration_source` names a sentence rather than a field. Appropriate here, with no document consequence.** The two base time eligibilities each govern one window whose length is a plan parameter, so a field locator exists. The six extended policies govern several windows of different lengths — one, two, three and twelve months — that are not plan parameters but are written into the rule sentences, so there is no field to name and "the window of calendar months named in the sentence that uses it" is the honest locator. On the document side it is moot twice: `duration_source` appears in no document of any product, and the duration travels **inside** every published window phrase, so each document is self-contained on it. Worth recording for the source layer only that the block is not mechanically resolvable to a value. Not a defect, and not a document matter.
